heading.en: Said is not the same as understood

hook.en: A manager says 'finish this soon'. One worker thinks it means today, another thinks next week. Most workplace problems start with a communication gap.

title.en: On the board: The communication process

narration.en: The sender has an idea and encodes it into words, symbols or gestures.

say.en: The sender has an idea and encodes it into words, symbols or gestures.
The message travels through a medium, is decoded, and reaches the receiver.
The receiver sends feedback to the sender, which completes the loop.
Noise is any disturbance, at any stage, that blocks or distorts the message.
Barriers are semantic, psychological, organisational and personal.

body.en: Formal communication follows the official chain of command: downward, upward, horizontal (lateral) or diagonal. Its networks are single chain, wheel, circular, free flow and inverted V. Informal communication, called the grapevine, arises from social interaction; its networks are single strand, gossip, probability and cluster. It spreads fast but may distort the message.

title.en: Barriers and how to overcome them

body.en: Semantic barriers come from words and symbols: badly expressed messages, words with many meanings, faulty translation, technical jargon, unclarified assumptions, body language. Psychological barriers: premature evaluation, lack of attention, loss in transmission, distrust. Organisational barriers: policy, rules, status, complex structure, poor facilities. Personal barriers: fear of challenge to authority, lack of confidence in subordinates, unwillingness to communicate, no incentives. Overcome them by clarifying ideas, communicating to the receiver's needs, consulting others, watching language and tone, getting feedback, following up and being a good listener.
body.kn: ಅಡೆತಡೆಗಳು ನಾಲ್ಕು ಬಗೆ: ಅರ್ಥ ಸಂಬಂಧಿ, ಮಾನಸಿಕ, ಸಾಂಸ್ಥಿಕ ಮತ್ತು ವೈಯಕ್ತಿಕ. ವಿಚಾರ ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಪಡಿಸುವುದು, ಪ್ರತಿಸ್ಪಂದನೆ ಪಡೆಯುವುದು, ಉತ್ತಮ ಕೇಳುಗರಾಗುವುದು ಇವುಗಳನ್ನು ನಿವಾರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

points.en: Personal: fear of challenge to authority

narration.en: Barriers are semantic, psychological, organisational and personal. Semantic barriers come from words and symbols, psychological ones from the state of mind, organisational ones from structure and rules, and personal ones from the attitudes of superiors and subordinates. We overcome them by clarifying ideas, getting feedback, following up and listening well.

problem.en: An English circular translated into Kannada by a clerk says 'the plant will be shut' where the original meant 'the plant (garden) near the gate will be removed'. Workers panic. Classify the barrier and suggest a remedy.

steps.en: The problem is in the meaning of words: 'plant' has two meanings and the translation was faulty.
Barriers related to words and symbols are semantic barriers.
Remedy: clarify the idea before communicating, use a competent translator and invite feedback.

answer.en: Semantic barrier (symbols with different meanings / faulty translation).
